newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on thin exports, positioning.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on thin exports, positioning.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower amid thin volume with positioning featured before the release at 0730 CDT Friday of USDA's October crop production and supply/demand reports, traders said.
Pressure also came from a lower-than-expected number in Thursday's USDA weekly export sales report, they said.
USDA early Thursday said U.S. wheat net export sales for the week ended October 3 were at 296,200 tonnes, 50 percent below the previous week and 40 percent below the four-week average.
Deferred months held firm relative to nearby December. The distant contracts were underpinned by concerns about delays in seeding portions of the U.S. soft red winter wheat crop, traders said.
A late soybean harvest this year in the eastern U.S. growing region was leading to the concerns about delays in the seeding of the wheat crop.
"There is a concern that they (farmers) won't be able to plant their wheat on time," said James Beuerlein, extension agronomist at Ohio State University earlier this week.
Wheat closed three cents per bushel lower to two higher, with December down three at $4.24 a bushel.

Wheat technical indicators appeared in flux with the relative strength index (RSI) for December closing at 42.490 points. An RSI of 30 or less is generally considered near oversold status while 70 and above is viewed as roughly in overbought territory.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 11,000 contracts, down from 11,818 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Refco Inc bought 100 March $4.30 calls and sold 100 March $4.00 puts at 3/4 cent and The Chicago Corp sold 100 March $4.00 calls at 24-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 3,500 contracts, down from 4,183 Wednesday.
